title: The Little Mouse Who Rang Early
markdown:
In a sunny place by a little creek was a village called Whispering Wind. The sky there was always a friendly blue. Every day was like a happy storybook, with sunshine and cheerful sounds.

Sunny was a puppy with fur the colour of a sunbeam, a bundle of golden fluff. His ears flopped when he ran, and his tail wagged super-fast, like a hummingbird’s wings. His most favourite thing in the whole world was to chase butterflies. Flutter, flutter went their pretty wings, painted as if a rainbow had sneezed. Zoom, zoom went Sunny’s happy paws across the soft green grass. Every day, as the sun climbed higher, painting the sky with soft oranges and pinks, Sunny would wait. His little nose twitched. He waited for the big village clock to chime. That chime meant a whole day of exciting smells and games.

Then there was Niko, a tall kind camel with gentle eyes that had seen many things. Niko loved his gentle naps. He snoozed in his cosy spot under the big shady willow tree, where the leaves whispered to him. And oh, how he loved his morning mint tea. Every single day, just as the sun began to warm the sleepy rooftops, Niko would yawn a big slow happy yawn that stretched from his long nose all the way to his soft sandy tail.

And Old Tom, the gardener. His hat was always a little bit tilted, as if sharing a giggle with the sky. His pockets were always full of tiny promising seeds. Old Tom loved to hum. He hummed to his proud roses, he hummed to his cheerful sunflowers, and he hummed to the little green shoots just peeking out of the dark damp soil. He coaxed them awake with his gentle tunes. Every day he waited for a special sound, a sound that told him the world was ready for his songs.

Whispering Wind had a very important clock, grand and old, standing tall in the village square, the heartbeat of their happy days. Inside that clock lived a very special little mouse named Pipkin. Pipkin was the clock-winder. He loved being on time more than cheese — and that is a lot for a little mouse. He would wake before the sun even thought about peeking over the hills. He’d tiptoe around the clock’s giant gears. He’d check every little spring and cog. He made sure everything was just right. He made sure the big shiny bell was ready to ring, precisely, at nine o’clock sharp. And that chime, that beautiful clear chime that echoed through the valley, was the signal for everyone to start their happy day.

Until one day was a little bit different.

Sunny woke, and the air was already alive with the flutter of wings. Morning dew still clung to the petals of the daisies and buttercups, making them sparkle like tiny diamonds. His tail thumped with excitement. He wanted to chase those butterflies, feel the cool wet grass tickle his paws, explore all the new smells the dew brought. But the big clock in the square had not chimed nine yet. It was still quiet. If only the bell would ring now, he thought. His nose nudged the cool damp earth. He gave a little hopeful thump with his tail.

Niko also woke a little earlier than usual. The air was still soft and cool, just perfect for his morning mint tea. He could almost smell the sweet calming scent of the mint leaves steeping. He imagined the warm steam curling up from his mug, tickling his long nose. If only the bell would ring now, he could have his lovely tea while the sun was still a gentle whisper.

And Old Tom was already out in his garden, hands dusted with rich dark soil. A tiny ladybug, seven perfect spots, perched on his thumb, exploring with its little feelers. A new rosebud, blush pink, was just starting to unfurl its delicate petals, shyly peeking out at the world. A happy hum bubbled up inside him, a tune just for the flowers. If the bell would ring now, he mused, eyes twinkling, he could sing his wake-up songs to the flowers before they were fully awake. They did so love a morning tune.

Because of that, Sunny, heart full of a puppy’s happy anticipation, padded toward the clock tower, floppy ears perked high. Because of that, Niko, moving with slow graceful dignity, made his way toward the village square, his soft hum a gentle melody. And because of that, Old Tom, humming his cheerful tune, also strolled toward the same spot, a happy smile on his face. They all arrived just as Pipkin was peeking out of the clock tower’s little window, tiny spectacles shining in the early light.

Pipkin saw them, all gathered there, looking up at the clock. “Goodness gracious!” His whiskers twitched with surprise. “It’s not nine o’clock yet! Not at all! The time isn’t right!”

Sunny wagged his tail so hard his whole body wiggled. He looked up with big hopeful puppy eyes. “The butterflies, Pipkin! They’re so sparkly and they’re dancing already!”

Niko gave a soft rumbling hum. “And the air is just right for a quiet cup of tea. So calm and peaceful.”

Old Tom smiled, a warm crinkly smile. “And these little buds,” he explained, pointing to a cluster of unopened flowers, “they’re almost ready to say hello to the day. They’d love to hear a song.”

Pipkin looked at Sunny’s bright wagging tail. He heard Niko’s soft rumbling hum. He felt the hopeful warmth of Old Tom’s smile. He looked at the big clock. Its hands were still a few minutes away from the important nine. He thought about his careful winding, his precise timing, his duty. Then he looked at his friends, hearts full of quiet anticipation, brimming with a special kind of early-morning joy.

Sometimes it is good to be precisely on time. Sometimes a little bit of early joy, a moment of unexpected happiness, is the sweetest thing of all. Like finding an extra sweet apple on a morning walk.

So Pipkin scurried to the bell rope. The thick worn rope hung down into the belfry. With a little grunt of effort and a happy wiggle, he pulled. The rope felt heavy, but his heart felt light. The bell rang out, not at nine, but just a little bit before. A cheerful welcoming sound.

Sunny yipped with pure delight and bounded into the dewy grass, happy barks echoing as he chased the dancing butterflies. Niko sat under his willow tree with his steaming cup of mint tea, a peaceful contented look on his gentle face. And Old Tom, heart full of a gardener’s joy, began to sing his quiet happy songs to the waking flowers. They seemed to unfurl a little bit faster to listen.

Ever since then, the bells of Whispering Wind have sometimes rung a little bit early, just for the joy of it, just for a special moment of shared happiness. Days often start with an extra happy chime.

Pipkin logged dew-diamonds / mint-steam / blush-rosebud in the winding book one minute early, left the nine o’clock mark its dignity, and let Sunny’s tail keep time with the butterflies. Some happy moments, he found, you do not want to wait for.
